title: Add .js runtime bridges to @moe/skills, @moe/mcp and @moe/control-room-client
description:
Objective: make @moe/skills, @moe/mcp and @moe/control-room-client loadable by plain Node. Created by architect-0b81de40 2026-08-09 from a measured probe. Same defect class as task-eb9ff081 (@moe/runner, fixed at 160215a), task-386fcb4c (@moe/core) and task-b7049554 (@moe/context + @moe/review).

THE DEFECT, MEASURED 2026-08-09 with working controls:
  ./packages/skills/src/index.ts              -> FAIL ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND :: '...skills/src/skill-contract.js'
  ./packages/mcp/src/index.ts                 -> FAIL ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND :: '...mcp/src/stdio/stdio-server.js'
  ./packages/control-room-client/src/index.ts -> FAIL ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND :: '...control-room-client/src/client-*.js'
Controls passing in the same sweep, proving the probe is valid: scheduler OK (36 exports), store OK (26), runner OK (66), contracts OK (46), coordination OK (14), testkit OK (11).

COUNTS: skills 5 non-test .ts / 0 .js; mcp 10 / 0; control-room-client 3 / 0. Eighteen bridges across three packages, one mechanical concern.

TWO THINGS THAT MAKE THIS ONE DIFFERENT FROM ITS SIBLING SWEEPS, and that the plan must handle explicitly:
  1. @moe/mcp has a SUBDIRECTORY (stdio/) and a third-party dependency (@modelcontextprotocol/sdk). Bridges are per-module regardless of depth, so stdio/ needs its own glob; and an external dependency in the import graph means the probe can fail for a reason that is NOT a missing bridge. Distinguish those: a failure naming a node_modules path is not this task's defect and should be reported, not "fixed" with a bridge.
  2. @moe/control-room-client contains GENERATED output (src/generated/generated-client.ts) plus generator-determinism and coverage tests. A generated module still needs a bridge, but the bridge is hand-written source that sits BESIDE generated output - do not add bridge creation to the generator, and do not hand-edit generated files. Confirm generator-determinism.test.ts still passes after the sweep.

Deliverable: the tracked one-line sibling bridge for every non-test module in all three packages - `export * from "./<name>.ts";` - one line, LF, trailing newline (mem:gotcha-scheduler-js-shims). Test files, *-test-fixtures.ts and *-test-helpers.ts get NO bridge.

NOT in scope: changing ANY behaviour; editing any .ts file including the index files; regenerating or hand-editing generated client output; adding a build step; any package.json or lockfile edit.

Hard dependencies: none.

Owned paths: packages/skills/src/**/*.js, packages/mcp/src/**/*.js, packages/control-room-client/src/**/*.js (new bridges only), and one new runtime-entrypoint test per package.
Verification: the focused typecheck and test command for each of the three packages, PLUS the plain-Node probe for all three - the vitest gates alone are NOT evidence for this task.
definitionOfDone: Every non-test .ts module in all three packages has a tracked sibling .js bridge whose entire content is the single line `export * from "./<name>.ts";` with LF and a trailing newline, including modules in subdirectories such as packages/mcp/src/stdio/. Test files and *-test-fixtures.ts / *-test-helpers.ts have none. An audit loop over all three reports zero MISSING and zero UNEXPECTED, raw output recorded.
The module set for each package was re-derived at task start rather than taken from this description, and the evidence states all three actual counts against the 5, 10 and 3 measured here.

A plain-Node probe from the repo ROOT proves ALL THREE entries load, with all three controls: POSITIVE (each resolves with more than zero exports), REGRESSION CONTROL (a known-good bridged package still loads), NEGATIVE CONTROL (a test-only path still raises the literal ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND). Covering two of three is incomplete evidence.

Any probe failure naming a path inside node_modules is reported as a separate finding, NOT worked around with a bridge — @moe/mcp depends on @modelcontextprotocol/sdk and an external resolution failure is a different defect with a different owner.
Every export of all three entry points is defined under Node semantics, not merely resolvable.

A runtime-entrypoint test per package spawns a real Node child with --experimental-strip-types importing the entry, asserting the import succeeded AND a named export is defined — never merely that the process exited 0.

packages/control-room-client's existing generator-determinism.test.ts and generated-coverage.test.ts still pass, proving the sweep did not disturb generated output; no generated file was hand-edited and the generator was not taught to emit bridges.

Zero behaviour change: git diff shows only added .js files plus the three new tests; no .ts file is modified. All three suites pass with counts greater than or equal to their pre-task counts, stated as explicit before/after numbers, and all focused gates exit 0.
taskRails: Bridges only. Do not edit a single .ts file, including the index files. If a bridge cannot be written without a .ts change, report_blocked.

A green vitest run is NOT evidence for this task — vitest resolves ./foo.js to foo.ts and is structurally blind to a missing bridge. Only the plain-Node probe counts, and only with its negative control passing.
The negative control must assert the literal ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND, never merely that an import failed.
Do not hand-edit generated output in packages/control-room-client/src/generated/, and do not modify the generator to emit bridges. A bridge is hand-written source that sits beside generated output.
A probe failure naming node_modules is NOT this task's defect. Report it; never paper over an external resolution failure with a bridge.
Bridge content is exact: one line, LF, trailing newline. Verify the written BYTES, not the apparent text.
Cover all three packages or none. A partial sweep is invisible to every vitest gate, which is precisely how this defect class survives.
Commit by explicit pathspec only, never a bare git commit — several agents share this working directory.

implementationPlan.description: Re-derive all three module sets and reproduce the three failures. Run `find packages/skills/src packages/mcp/src packages/control-room-client/src -name '*.ts' -not -name '*.test.ts'` and record exact counts against the 5, 10 and 3 measured when this task was written. CRITICALLY, identify the test-only modules: `packages/mcp/src/http/http-server-test-helpers.ts` matches the `*-test-helpers.ts` convention and must get NO bridge, which makes the real bridge count 5 + 9 + 3 = 17 rather than 18 — confirm that on disk and re-check whether any further test-helper or fixture module has appeared. Note the directory structure, because a top-level-only sweep would silently miss seven bridges: mcp has `http/` and `stdio/`, control-room-client has `generated/`. Reproduce the defect with a valid probe on all three entries, expecting ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND naming `skill-contract.js`, `stdio/stdio-server.js` and a `client-*.js`, and run a KNOWN-GOOD control in the same breath — without it a cwd mistake looks exactly like the defect. Read `packages/core/src/identity/identity-session.js` with `cat -A` to confirm the exact bridge bytes. Produce no code.
implementationPlan.note:
Step 1 done. No code produced. Two plan-affecting discoveries.

MODULE SETS RE-DERIVED ON DISK (find, non-test .ts) — all three match the description exactly:
  skills              all_ts=7  nontest_ts=5   js_on_disk=0   (measured 5 -> confirmed 5)
  mcp                 all_ts=16 nontest_ts=10  js_on_disk=0   (measured 10 -> confirmed 10)
  control-room-client all_ts=6  nontest_ts=3   js_on_disk=0   (measured 3 -> confirmed 3)
Directories: skills flat; mcp = src/, src/http/, src/stdio/; control-room-client = src/, src/generated/. All three package.json pin an EXCLUSIVE exports map {".": "./src/index.ts"}, so the reachability rule from mem:gotcha-core-bridge-set-needs-reachability-not-name-or-closure is applicable here.

DEFECT REPRODUCED, plain Node v24.16.0 from repo root, per-entry separate processes:
  SUBJECT skills    IMPORT_FAILED ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND file:///D:/projexts/moe-next/packages/skills/src/skill-contract.js
  SUBJECT mcp       IMPORT_FAILED ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND file:///D:/projexts/moe-next/packages/mcp/src/stdio/stdio-server.js
  SUBJECT crc       IMPORT_FAILED ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND file:///D:/projexts/moe-next/packages/control-room-client/src/client-compat.js
KNOWN-GOOD CONTROLS in the same sweep (proves it is not a cwd mistake): scheduler IMPORTED 36/0 undefined, store 26/0, runner 66/0, core 39/0, contracts 46/0. All reproduce the plan-time numbers.
NEGATIVE CONTROL already valid pre-fix: http-server-test-helpers.js -> ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND.
No probe failure named a node_modules path. @modelcontextprotocol/sdk resolves fine — the mcp failure is a missing bridge at packages/mcp/src/stdio/stdio-server.js, inside the repo. Nothing to report under DoD 4 so far.

BRIDGE BYTES CONFIRMED by od on packages/core/src/identity/identity-session.js: 39 bytes, `export * from "./identity-session.ts";` + 0a, no 0d.

BEFORE test counts (all exit 0): skills 2 files / 75 passed + 1 skipped; mcp 6 files / 125 passed; control-room-client 3 files / 26 passed.

DISCOVERY 1 — THE BRIDGE COUNT IS 16, NOT 17. The plan says mcp gets 9, excluding only http/http-server-test-helpers.ts. A second mcp module is test-only and must also be skipped: packages/mcp/src/dispatch-conformance.ts imports { describe, expect, it } from "vitest" at module scope and is referenced ONLY by five *.test.ts files (http-parity, http-server-lifecycle, http-server, stdio-server tests) plus one prose comment. It is a test-tier module with no test suffix — exactly mem:gotcha-test-tier-modules-have-no-test-suffix, and exactly the class the @moe/core sweep deliberately left unbridged. Bridging it would publish a vitest import on the runtime surface, which task rail "Never bridge a test-only module" forbids and which no downstream gate would complain about. So: skills 5 + mcp 8 + control-room-client 3 = 16. I will make dispatch-conformance a SECOND negative control in step 5 rather than a bridge. Flagging because it contradicts the plan's explicit "nine bridges, NOT ten".

DISCOVERY 2 — A TRACKED TEST NAMES THIS TASK AS ITS ALLOWLIST OWNER. tests/runtime/package-loadability.test.ts (tracked, landed in a6e46f6) holds allowedPackageFailures entries for @moe/skills, @moe/mcp and @moe/control-room-client, each with ownerTaskId: "task-17b03331e4ee488a994635144cae4a53". tests/runtime/package-loadability-support.ts:243 emits "<pkg>: allowlist entry is stale" the moment a package IMPORTS while still allowlisted. So the instant my bridges land, that test goes RED unless the three entries are removed in the same commit. The allowance names my task as owner, so retiring it is this task's designed handoff, but the file is outside the paths enumerated in the task description — recording the scope addition explicitly rather than silently widening. Will announce in channel before committing.

implementationPlan.description: Sweep @moe/skills and @moe/mcp, honouring the exclusion. For every non-test module create the sibling `.js` whose ENTIRE content is `export * from "./<name>.ts";` — one line, LF, trailing newline. skills is flat (5 bridges). mcp spans three directories and needs all of them: `src/` (dispatch-conformance, index), `src/http/` (http-resume, http-server, http-session, http-tool-bridge) and `src/stdio/` (stdio-dispatch-port, stdio-server, stdio-tool-schemas) — nine bridges, NOT ten. **`src/http/http-server-test-helpers.ts` gets NO bridge**; bridging it would drag test-only code onto the runtime surface, and a naive `for each .ts` loop is exactly how that happens. Do not edit any `.ts` file, including either index.ts. If you script this, verify the written BYTES afterwards — editors and in-place scripts on Windows flip LF to CRLF and `git diff --stat` will not reveal it.

Sweep @moe/control-room-client, including its generated module, without disturbing generation. Create bridges for `src/client-compat.ts`, `src/index.ts` and `src/generated/generated-client.ts` — three bridges across two directories. The generated module DOES need a bridge, but that bridge is HAND-WRITTEN SOURCE sitting beside generated output: do NOT hand-edit `generated-client.ts` itself, and do NOT modify the generator to emit bridges — a generator that emits its own bridge would make the bridge regenerable output rather than tracked source, and would drift the moment the generator changes. Immediately afterwards run the package's existing `generator-determinism.test.ts` and `generated-coverage.test.ts` and confirm both still pass; they exist precisely to catch a disturbance to generated output, and they are the cheapest possible proof that this step was surgical.

Audit all three sweeps in BOTH directions. Loop over every directory of all three packages reporting, for each non-test .ts module, whether its sibling .js exists (zero MISSING), and whether any .js exists without a corresponding non-test .ts (zero UNEXPECTED). The UNEXPECTED direction matters more here than in the sibling sweeps: it is what catches `http-server-test-helpers.js` if the exclusion was missed, so assert explicitly that NO bridge exists for that module. Assert bridge CONTENT is exact for every file — one line, the correct sibling name, LF, trailing newline — since a bridge naming a neighbour resolves to the wrong module and passes an existence-only check. Record the loop's RAW OUTPUT and all three module counts in the evidence, confirming they match step 1.

The plain-Node probe with all three controls, across all three packages. Run from the repo ROOT. (a) POSITIVE: all three entries resolve, each with more than zero exports — covering two of three is incomplete evidence. (b) REGRESSION CONTROL: a known-good bridged package elsewhere still loads, proving the harness works so a broken probe cannot masquerade as a passing sweep. (c) NEGATIVE CONTROL: importing `packages/mcp/src/http/http-server-test-helpers.js` must STILL raise the LITERAL `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` — assert that exact code, never merely that an import failed. This control is unusually strong here because it is a real file that was deliberately left unbridged, so one assertion proves both that the probe can detect failure and that the exclusion was honoured. THEN THE DISCRIMINATION THAT MATTERS: if any probe fails naming a path inside `node_modules`, that is NOT this task's defect — @moe/mcp depends on @modelcontextprotocol/sdk, an external resolution failure has a different owner and a different fix, and it must be reported as a separate finding rather than papered over with a bridge. Finally assert every export of each entry point is DEFINED, not merely that the import resolved, since ESM cycles resolve differently per entry point and vitest never exercised them.

Add the three regression guards. Create one runtime-entrypoint test per package following the `packages/scheduler/src/scheduler-runtime-entrypoint.test.ts` precedent: spawn a REAL Node child or worker with `--experimental-strip-types` importing the package entry. Each must assert BOTH that the import succeeded AND that a specific named export is defined — never merely that the process exited 0, which is the weak assertion that let this defect class survive across six packages. For control-room-client, prefer asserting `createCompatGate` is defined, since it is the package's actual public entry point rather than an incidental symbol. These three tests are what make the fix durable: without them the next module added to any of these packages without a bridge silently reintroduces the defect.

Prove zero behaviour change, run all three gates, adversarially review, then commit. Confirm with `git status --porcelain` and `git diff --stat` that the diff contains ONLY added `.js` files plus the three new tests — no `.ts` file modified anywhere, and in particular nothing under `src/generated/`. Record each suite's test count BEFORE and AFTER as explicit numbers, all after-counts greater than or equal to their before-counts. Run all three focused gates (typecheck and test for skills, mcp and control-room-client) fresh, exiting 0 — while remembering this green run is NOT the evidence for this task; the step-5 probe is, and both must be reported. Adversarial pass: does `http-server-test-helpers.js` exist anywhere (it must NOT); does every bridge point at its own sibling; did any file get CRLF; does the negative control assert the literal ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND; do generator-determinism and generated-coverage still pass; was any probe failure naming node_modules quietly bridged instead of reported; did a concurrent task add a module after step 1 — re-run the audit immediately before committing. Then commit by EXPLICIT PATHSPEC covering the new .js files and the three tests: never a bare git commit, never git add -A, never a directory pathspec under packages/. Verify with `git show --stat` that no .ts file appears.

planSizeWarnings: Plan touches 9 distinct files (target <=5); plans over 10 are rejected. Small file-disjoint tasks review better and parallelize.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
(1) THREE PACKAGES, ONE TASK — justified because it is one mechanical concern with one probe harness, and the three are individually tiny (5, 10 and 3 modules). But this is the LEAST uniform of the three sweep tasks and the plan says so explicitly: @moe/mcp has two subdirectories and a third-party dependency, and @moe/control-room-client contains generated output. Those two wrinkles get their own steps rather than being buried in a bulk sweep.
(2) THE EXCLUSION RULE HAS A REAL TARGET HERE, unlike its sibling task. `packages/mcp/src/http/http-server-test-helpers.ts` matches the `*-test-helpers.ts` convention and must get NO bridge. That is also the natural aim for the probe's negative control: after the sweep, importing `http-server-test-helpers.js` must STILL fail with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND, which simultaneously proves the probe can detect failure and that test-only files were correctly skipped. The sibling task had to invent a non-existent specifier for this; here the real thing exists.
(3) GENERATED OUTPUT GETS A HAND-WRITTEN BRIDGE. `src/generated/generated-client.ts` still needs `generated-client.js` beside it, but the bridge is hand-written source — do NOT teach the generator to emit bridges and do NOT hand-edit generated files. The package already ships generator-determinism and generated-coverage tests that will catch either mistake.
(4) EXTERNAL DEPENDENCY FAILURES ARE NOT THIS TASK'S DEFECT. @moe/mcp depends on @modelcontextprotocol/sdk; a probe failure naming node_modules is a different defect with a different owner and must be reported, never papered over with a bridge.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
MODULE SETS ENUMERATED ON DISK 2026-08-09 — re-derive at step 1, but exact as of now.
**packages/skills/src (5 modules, 0 bridges, FLAT):** index.ts, skill-contract.ts, skill-loader.ts, skill-manifest.ts, skill-snapshot.ts.
**packages/mcp/src (10 modules, 0 bridges, THREE directories):** root — dispatch-conformance.ts, index.ts; `http/` — http-resume.ts, http-server.ts, http-session.ts, http-tool-bridge.ts, AND **http-server-test-helpers.ts which is TEST-ONLY and gets NO bridge**; `stdio/` — stdio-dispatch-port.ts, stdio-server.ts, stdio-tool-schemas.ts.
**packages/control-room-client/src (3 modules, 0 bridges, TWO directories):** root — client-compat.ts, index.ts; `generated/` — generated-client.ts (GENERATED OUTPUT).
So the bridge count is 5 + 9 + 3 = 17, not 18: one of mcp's ten modules is the test-helper that must be skipped.
**Measured failures with valid controls:** skills -> ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND on `skill-contract.js`; mcp -> on `stdio/stdio-server.js`; control-room-client -> on a `client-*.js`. Controls passing in the same sweep: scheduler(36 exports), store(26), runner(66), contracts(46), coordination(14), testkit(11).
**Bridge form, confirmed by `cat -A` on packages/core/src/identity/*.js:** exactly `export * from "./<name>.ts";` plus a newline — one line, LF, trailing newline.
**control-room-client already ships** `client-compat.test.ts`, `generated-coverage.test.ts` and `generator-determinism.test.ts`; its index exports `createCompatGate`. Those existing tests are the guard that catches any disturbance to generated output.
**@moe/mcp dependencies:** @moe/contracts and @modelcontextprotocol/sdk — the only package in this sweep with a third-party dependency.
**Precedent for the regression test:** `packages/scheduler/src/scheduler-runtime-entrypoint.test.ts`.
**Bridges are committed source, not build output**: tsconfig sets noEmit with `include: ["src/**/*.ts"]`, so tsc never typechecks them and they are not gitignored.
planningNotes.risks:
1. **A GREEN VITEST RUN IS NOT EVIDENCE FOR THIS TASK.** vitest rewrites `./foo.js` to `foo.ts` and is structurally blind to a missing bridge. Only the plain-Node probe counts, and only with its negative control passing.
2. **The test-helper is the trap AND the opportunity.** `mcp/src/http/http-server-test-helpers.ts` must get NO bridge; a bulk `for each .ts` loop that forgets the exclusion will bridge it and drag test-only code onto the runtime surface. Use it as the negative control afterwards.
3. **An external resolution failure is not a missing bridge.** @moe/mcp depends on @modelcontextprotocol/sdk; if the probe fails naming a node_modules path, report it as a separate finding — adding a bridge would not fix it and would disguise it.
4. **Do not touch generated output.** Do not hand-edit `src/generated/generated-client.ts` and do not modify the generator to emit bridges. Confirm `generator-determinism.test.ts` and `generated-coverage.test.ts` still pass after the sweep — they exist precisely to catch this.
5. **Subdirectories need their own globs.** mcp/src, mcp/src/http, mcp/src/stdio, control-room-client/src, control-room-client/src/generated. A sweep that only walks the top level silently misses seven of the seventeen bridges, and that incompleteness is invisible to every vitest gate.
6. **Resolution is not re-export**, and **undefined bindings are the cycle symptom**: assert non-empty namespaces for value modules and that every export of each entry point is DEFINED, not merely that the import resolved.
7. **Line endings on Windows**: verify the written BYTES, not the apparent text — `git diff --stat` will not show an LF-to-CRLF flip.
8. Commit hazard: several agents share this working directory. Commit by explicit pathspec, never a directory under packages/.
